page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable strength, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth for both read and write operations, along with static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations, also registers average performance. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M models and strong performance on medium 7B models.

With dedicated CPU allocation and a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a compute-focused resource profile. The inclusion of local NVMe storage provides a balanced configuration for workloads requiring fast local disk access without the overhead of external network storage. This server is suited for compute-intensive tasks, text processing pipelines, lightweight LLM inference, web serving, and general-purpose application hosting where dedicated CPU resources are required.
